checks.sources_say: Customer email states 'Policy number: VER-1004'; Policy Schedule confirms policy_id VER-1004 for holder Thomas Petit.
checks.evidence: Customer email signature block; Policy Schedule in claims system.

checks.sources_say: Email describes damage to the policyholder's own car after reversing into a concrete pillar — a collision damaging the insured vehicle, which is C2 'Collision damage' per contract Article 2; C2 is listed in the Policy Schedule coverages.
checks.evidence: Customer email body ('I hit a concrete pillar'); contract Article 2 coverage table (document 2630#10414, page 1); Policy Schedule coverages [C1, C2].

checks.sources_say: Email: 'an accident that happened on 03 October 2026'.
Email received on 2026-10-04 reporting the accident.

Email: 'The garage quoted €900 to repair my car.' The quote itself (repair_quote.pdf) is stored by the mailroom and cannot be opened, so the total-incl.-VAT line per Article 1 cannot be inspected directly, but no source contradicts €900.
checks.evidence: Customer email, third paragraph; contract Article 1 definition of repair cost (document 2630#10414, page 1).

checks.sources_say: Email: policyholder was reversing and hit the pillar himself; 'Nobody else was involved' — the authorised driver caused the damage, so at fault.
Email: 'Nobody else was involved.' A concrete pillar is not a third party (Article 1: third party = any person other than the authorised driver).
checks.evidence: Customer email, second paragraph; contract Article 1 definition (document 2630#10414, page 1).

checks.sources_say: No third party exists, so none is identified; consistent with the email.

Email attachments damage_photos.zip and repair_quote.pdf, both also stored by the mailroom and counted as received; both belong to this claim (policy VER-1004, Thomas Petit's vehicle). Article 4.3 requires for C2: photos of the damage and repair quote (accident report only when a third party is involved — not the case here).
checks.evidence: Customer email attachment list; mailroom storage note; contract Article 4.3 required-documents table (document 2630#10414, page 2).

checks.sources_say: Nothing in the email or documents indicates any Article 3 exclusion (no alcohol/drugs, licence held since 2008-11-01 so valid, no racing, damage not intentional, not wear/mechanical failure).
checks.evidence: Customer email (no exclusion facts stated); contract Article 3 exclusions (document 2630#10414, page 2); Policy Schedule licence_date.

verdict.summary: All recorded facts match the customer email and the Veridia contract; the claim was reported within the 5-day deadline, C2 collision coverage is in the Policy Schedule, required documents are provided, no exclusion applies, and no playbook referral rule is triggered, so the staged payment of €600 (€900 repair cost minus €300 deductible) should be approved.
